content: Biqu Cryogrip build plates will no longer work.  The build plate covers the wiper. You can cut off the front part of the build plate.

The next step after installing the holder to the Z-carriage is to apply the adhesive-backed wiper onto the holder. The order of this makes no sense to me. It is MUCH easier to apply the wiper to the holder BEFORE attaching the holder to the Z-carriage. It’s what I did and I would recommend you do it this way as well, as it caused no issue and undoubtedly removed a little frustration from the process.

The expansion joint screw cracks the part pretty much no matter what. Not sure how they thought this was appropriate to sell. It's even cracked in the picture they're showing. Mine cracked before the screw was even seated all the way. Terrible.

replies.content: If you choose to reprint the part and try again, see my comment on the previous step. Pre-threading the hole with the screw will help prevent the part from cracking.

content: Left end rises because the hole don't line up correctly forcing the plastic wiper hard against the steel that the little hook is on and forcing the wiper to bend up
This is confusing with the INDX upgrade

Early Core One kit. The hole for the screw seems to line up ok, but the left end rises up by about a mm.

I'm going to go with it and see what happens.

replies.content: The left side of mine rose by about 1mm as well, once the screw was sufficiently snug. While this annoys my anal-retentive brain, it may actually be a “feature,” since it will be pushing more of the wiper material into the nozzle on that side; give it a little extra-firm scrub!

content: The screw is slightly too short, in order for it to grasp the plastic in the nut (which is there to prevent the screw from loosening) .

replies.content: In my case, the M3x10 screw was flush with the top surface of the nylon ring in the M3nN nut once sufficiently tightened. Perhaps your nut wasn’t fully seated in the pocket? I believe the rule of thumb is you want 2-4 threads visible past the locking feature of the nut, but… This isn’t a fighter jet, so… I think it’ll be fine.

content: Do NOT tighten the screw to tight mine cracked because of tightening it to tight.

This was a pretty tight fit for me. Getting the screw hole aligned with the frame was rough, looked like it was off by a fraction of a mm, but I was able to hold it in place with some force and get the screw threaded through.

Similar to Cu3885, I see the tab on the far end lifting a bit, but it's unclear to me if this is by design.
We have one of the first core one kits and the whole on the nozzle wiper holder is slightly misaligned which was causing it to lift up on the far end (away from the nut and bolt) when tightened down.

replies.content: Hello. Please contact our support team.

Same for me, though i would not say it is a alignment issue for me. I have a gap of 0,5mm to 1mm between the part where the nut is in and the mounting  point on the arm of the heat bed. This causes the left part of the wiper to rise when I tighten the bolt.
